summary:
Tacna stands under Peru's national framework; national law on criminalisation, anti-discrimination protection, identity documents and public-facility access applies here as it does across the country and is set out under Peru.

On 19 April 2025 Marcia Paucara Cora, a 48-year-old trans woman, was found dead in a room of the Los 5 Titos hostel on Arias y Aragüez street in central Tacna. The autopsy recorded death by mechanical asphyxia through compression of the airways. She had entered the hostel with a man who registered under a false identity and who left alone roughly two hours later carrying a white bag. Staff found the body when the rental time expired.

Tacna authorities are investigating the death as a possible hate crime, an offence motivated by prejudice and discrimination on grounds of the victim's sexual orientation or gender identity. No suspect had been identified in the reporting of 21 and 27 May 2025. The victim was initially processed as an unidentified body and was named through the hostel's cameras; police were analysing surveillance footage from inside and outside the premises to trace the suspect's escape route.

Family members and local LGTBIQ+ collectives held a vigil on Friday 23 May 2025 demanding justice, describing the killing as the reflection of a structural system of violence that silences trans lives. Relatives publicly denounced the killing and pressed for police action.
tangentialFactors:
The Tacna investigation depends on commercial surveillance. The victim was unidentified when her body was found and was named through the hostel's cameras, and the suspect's route is being reconstructed from footage inside and outside the premises. He registered under a false identity, so no verified name for him has been established.

The killing is the region's documented trans-specific homicide of the period. National figures on anti-trans violence and the state of national hate-crime law sit with the Peru entry and are not restated here.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of Tacna live under the same national legal framework as the rest of Peru, with no regional protection or restriction identified in the sources.

Local LGTBIQ+ collectives in Tacna organised the vigil of 23 May 2025 and are pressing the authorities for justice; the victim's relatives publicly denounced the killing and demanded police action.
outOfScopeNotes:
No suspect had been identified and no arrest reported as of the May 2025 coverage; the outcome of the Tacna investigation is not sourced.

Whether the case is formally classified and prosecuted as a hate crime is unresolved. The man who entered the hostel with the victim registered under a false identity, and mechanical asphyxia is the only recorded cause of death.
